subject.title: Feature Request: Support YAML as config file format

question: Should OpenClaw expand the stable core config contract to accept `openclaw.yaml`/`openclaw.yml`, or keep JSON/JSON5 canonical and solve the reported editing friction through CLI, Control UI, and `config.patch` guidance?
rationale: The request changes a stable on-disk config contract and needs human product ownership for parser dependency, precedence, write-back, validation, and upgrade semantics.

options.title: Keep JSON/JSON5 canonical
options.body: Treat YAML as out of scope for now and improve the supported comment-aware mutation paths instead.

options.title: Design YAML support
options.body: Sponsor YAML only with explicit parser semantics, precedence rules, docs, fresh-install proof, and upgrade/doctor tests.

options.title: Split mutation guidance
options.body: Track a narrower docs or agent-prompt issue for avoiding raw parse-and-dump edits without adding another config file format.

recommendation.title: Keep JSON/JSON5 canonical
recommendation.body: Treat YAML as out of scope for now and improve the supported comment-aware mutation paths instead.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision turns on config compatibility, doctor migration, and recovery policy, where history points strongly to this owner area.
